questiontext.text:
The data for this question are monthly total sunshine hours for 30 years from a single station and from satellite estimates close to that station. There are four columns in the data: year, month, sunh and sunh_sat.

sunh are the station values and sunh_sat are the satellite values.

Click the button to download the data in CSV format. Then import the data into R-Instat (or your favourite statistics package).

Calculate the mean error (bias) for each month.

1. What is the mean error in {@month_ran_text@}?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

2. In which month does the mean bias indicate that the satellite values are giving the closest estimates to the station data on average?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

[[feedback:prt2]]

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text:
Not quite! Your answer has the right value but the wrong sign, so you did the right calculation but probably with the columns the wrong way round.

Normally, mean error is defined as: mean(estimates - observations).

So you should have got {@ta1_dp@} as your answer.

You might need to check how to interpret the mean error. You chose the month where the mean bias was furthest from {@0@}, so this is the month where the satellite values are furthest from the station values. When the satellite values are closest to the station values, the mean error is close to {@0@}.
